question: Does letting the model keep its code as named routines the harness runs, and sleep until something wakes it, cost less per level than the snippet loop on the fixed loop, without slowing progress?
note: The program spike's first round (operator, 2026-11-12), on the spike branch only: nothing of it merges before the spike is adopted. Three arms on one image built from the spike branch, so harness drift cannot separate them: snippet passes no loop flag and runs the snippet loop byte for byte as the release does (prompt, tools, config and tuple); program passes --loop program, which serves the program's file and routine tools, makes a reply with no tool call sleep until a wake (a routine ending, the first error or refusal of a signature since a load, a wake() call, a death, the stream closing, a sandbox restart, a harness notice) or five minutes, and opens the next requests with a facts-only [wake] block; program-yield adds --yield true, a yield tool held open until a wake. A program-arm run records loop (and yield) in its config and its comparability tuple; a snippet-arm run records neither. All three arms pin, by tag and digest, the probe image built from the spike branch at 69e5b57 (stack ed0c7b6); an image without --loop would refuse the flag and spend the square. One cell, human-paladin. A 90-minute clock with idle at 20 minutes, no no-XP watchdog and no stopping level, so every run reaches its 60- and 90-minute cuts; the 3000-call guard is e90's and the fixed loop does not read it. resume is false: a paused run is a spent attempt. Assignments are the store row's: one roster entry, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on the openrouter-v1 credential with routing pinned to DeepSeek, on all three arms; round 1 is one run per arm started together, round 2 the same again.

cells.note: The start the earlier entrypoint spike ran from.

arms.note: The control: the spike image with no loop flag, the snippet loop as released.
Routines in a file workspace, run by the harness; a reply with no tool call sleeps until a wake.
The program arm, plus a yield tool whose call is held open until a wake and returns it.
